learning.why: The teacher's hint 'Fourteen is one ___' and the child's prior success with 'one ten' helped the child label it right.

end.summary:
Practised representing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and some loose sticks.
Saanvi identified ten sticks as one bundle.
They stated thirteen as ten and three, and fourteen as ten and four.
They briefly said “ten teen” and corrected it to “thirteen.”
Teach-back was not completed; Saanvi became tired and stopped the lesson.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised making numbers with one bundle of ten and loose ones. They used the stick method to state thirteen as ten and three, and fourteen as ten and four; the brief “ten teen” mix-up was corrected to “thirteen” later in the lesson. At home, try making 11–20 with small objects and ask once, “How many tens and how many ones?”
